title: Beatrix and the Alibi
premise: When archivist Vesper Vasquez receives a confession letter for a murder that happened ten years ago — postmarked the day after the victim's funeral — they realize the letter was written by someone who has read the sealed case file only they curate. As Vesper quietly investigates, they discover the confession is a trap: the real killer is using Vesper's own archive to frame a dying man and burn the evidence before the statute of limitations expires. Vesper must reconstruct the true night of the murder from catalogued fragments, confront the cathedral's beloved dean whose power the crime protected, and stage a final exhibition of evidence that forces a confession before the clock runs out.
about_author: Dominic Nystrom is a former parish records clerk from the upper Midwest who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was supposed to read. His fiction explores what institutions bury and what it costs the people paid to hold the shovel.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ten days after Mayor Edith Calloway's funeral, a yellowed envelope arrives at the cathedral addressed in a dead woman's handwriting, confessing to the 2014 drowning of a boy named Tomas Reyes. Vesper, who filed the original case, recognizes the paper stock as archival — their own. The beat is cold dread: someone has been inside the locked crypt.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper audits the crypt's holdings and finds the Tomas Reyes file intact but subtly reordered — a page swapped, a date corrected. Detective Ansel Okafor, now retiring, visits to donate his old case notes and mentions the statute expires in six weeks. Beat: the unsettling realization that the archive itself is a crime scene.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Signature
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The confession is signed by Wendell Marsh, Edith's business partner, who is in hospice with weeks to live. Vesper visits him; Marsh is lucid but terrified, insisting he never wrote any letter and never confessed to anyone. Beat: sympathy curdling into suspicion — someone wants a dead man to take the fall.

chapters.title: What the Dean Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dean Cassian Whitlock, the cathedral's magnetic leader and Edith's confidant, gently warns Vesper that reopening old wounds serves no one. He reveals the crypt's lock was changed two years ago at his instruction. Beat: loyalty tested — Vesper likes Cassian, and that is exactly what makes him dangerous.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, interleaved with recovered documents. Flashback fragments reconstruct Tomas Reyes: a sixteen-year-old altar server who drowned in the reservoir the night of the 2014 capital campaign gala. The file shows Edith's car was towed from the reservoir road at 1 a.m. Beat: grief for a boy the town chose to forget.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A second letter arrives — this one threatening Vesper by name, quoting their private accession notes verbatim. Only three people ever saw those notes. One is dead, one is dying, and one is the Dean. Beat: fear sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Okafor's Regret
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Okafor. The retired detective admits he closed the case under pressure from above — the DA wanted the gala season clean. He kept a duplicate evidence log he never filed. Beat: guilt as fuel; an ally with a conscience and nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Swapped Page
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Forensic comparison shows the altered archive page was typed on the cathedral's own 1990s typewriter, still in the Dean's office. The frame is being built inside the building Vesper guards. Beat: betrayal — the institution is complicit in its own cover-up.

chapters.title: Edith's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Among Edith's donated papers, Vesper finds a coded ledger: payments routed to Tomas's family for a decade, stopping the month she died. Was she paying penance — or being paid to stay quiet? Beat: the victim's image fractures; Edith was both witness and accomplice.

chapters.title: Marsh Slips
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Marsh in hospice. Under sedation he murmurs about 'the water' and 'the Dean's car.' A nurse, Rosa, contacts Vesper. Beat: urgency — the frame's intended defendant is losing the time to defend himself.

chapters.title: The Reservoir at Night
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper and Okafor walk the old towpath, reconstructing the 2014 timeline. A storm drain grate, rusted open in old photos, was welded shut the week after the gala. Beat: the geography of the crime confirms someone with authority sealed the town's memory shut.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The cathedral board, pressed by Cassian, suspends Vesper for 'procedural irregularities' and seizes the crypt keys. Rosa is fired the same day. Beat: isolation — the machinery of institutional power closing ranks, showing how corruption protects itself.

chapters.title: The Duplicate Log
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor hands Vesper his unfiled duplicate log: a missing item from 2014 evidence — Tomas's scuffed locket — was signed out by a junior clerk named Cassian Whitlock. Beat: the revelation lands like a struck bell.

chapters.title: What Vesper Filed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with memory interludes. Vesper confronts their own decade of complicity: they catalogued the anomalies, noticed the gaps, and chose order over questions. Beat: the theme turns inward — memory as moral duty, and the cost of having looked away.

chapters.title: Rosa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Rosa. She recalls Marsh's ravings in full: he drove Edith's car to the reservoir that night because Cassian summoned him, and he has carried the guilt while Cassian rose. Beat: the confession letter was real in origin — dictated by a dying man and weaponized by his listener.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper realizes the killer's plan: let the statute expire with Marsh framed, then burn the crypt's Reyes holdings during a scheduled 'deaccession.' Vesper lets a doctored file leak to bait Cassian into moving early. Beat: the hunted becomes the hunter.

chapters.title: Smoke in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, night. The crypt alarm trips; smoke, an intruder, a struggle in the dark stacks. Vesper traps the intruder — the Dean's assistant, Halvard — with the typewriter and the locket in his bag. Beat: adrenaline and near-defeat as Halvard swears he was only following orders.

chapters.title: The Dean's Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Confronted with the locket, the ledger, and Halvard's statement, Cassian finally breaks — not with remorse but with justification: Tomas's death was an accident of panic, and a decade of the cathedral's good work was worth one boy's silence. Beat: the theme made flesh — power narrating its own innocence.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. With two days left, Okafor files everything: the duplicate log, the ledger, the letters' typewriter forensics, Cassian's recorded statement. Marsh, moved to the hospice's common room, gives a formal dying declaration. Beat: racing the clock, the machinery of justice finally engaging.

chapters.title: Exhibit A
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper mounts a public exhibition in the cathedral nave: the true file, unredacted, under the title 'Tomas Reyes, 1998–2014.' The town reads its own buried memory in the pews where it was taught to forget. Beat: catharsis — truth displayed where power preached.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Vesper and Okafor. Cassian resigns under indictment; the DA, once complicit, recuses rather than face the file. Marsh dies peacefully, his name cleared, Rosa at his side. Beat: justice partial and imperfect — the system bends only as far as it must.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, final chapter. Reinstated, Vesper refiles the Reyes archive — not under 'closed' but under 'ongoing' — and adds their own accession note confessing ten years of silence. The last letter in the drawer is one Vesper writes to Tomas. Beat: quiet resolve; memory kept is loyalty finally earned.
